name: Terrace Cottage
description: Located in one of Asheville's oldest historic districts, walkable to UNC-Asheville, the Omni Grove Park Inn, restaurants, wine shops, markets, greenways, parks and more! Downtown is walkable on well-lit sidewalks (under 2 miles), a 5-min drive away.
host_about:
Welcome to Terrace Cottage!

For fifteen years we have enjoyed hosting visitors in our Asheville, North Carolina cottage from across the country and around the world including England and Ireland, Greece, Canada, Mexico and Cuba, Argentina, Japan and The Phillipines. We welcome guests from around the corner, across the US and our international visitors as well! Our college-age daughter grew up listening to many different languages in the driveway.

We enjoy traveling including work-and-play trips to Ireland, England, Sweden and Greece. Twenty years here at our residence built in 1926 and our adjacent Terrace Cottage was built in 2000.

We love working in our perennial beds and veggie gardens.

I'm an online entrepreneur designing and marketing wooden playthings for young people. I also collect and blog about vintage wooden toys.

My wife is a clinician with UNC-Chapel Hill School of Medicine. 

We love living in Asheville and are always happy to return home when away. It is a nationally-celebrated and uniquely beautiful mountain city overflowing with eclectic opportunities for enjoying first-rate dining, entertainment, crafts and artwork. The Blue Ridge Parkway entrance is ten minutes from our home, leading to the North Carolina Arboretum, Mount Pisgah, Craggy Gardens, and Mount Mitchell- the highest elevation east of the Rocky Mountains. 

I fly fish and welcome inquiries regarding our local waters. My favorite streams are under an hour away and have been rated in Trout Unlimited's Top 100. There are excellent fly shops and outfitters nearby if you need them.

Walking, running and cycling are huge in Asheville and there are too many options to mention from neighborhood greenways and hill climbs to maniacal day-longs as well, contact us for info. Our local runner's and cyclist's shops are just blocks away.

Speaking of walkable- ditto our supermarket and specialty/whole foods markets, cafes, coffee shops, local theater, pharmacies, UNC-Asheville, botanical gardens, awesome kid's parks and more.

Thanks for looking at Terrace Cottage and we welcome your inquiries!

Being a massage therapist there, I can tell you which treatments will be perfect for you.  I have spent plenty of time at the Biltmore Estates and can suggest good walks to take there.

host_about:
I am a singer/songwriter, voice talent, and amateur gardener. I love the arts, eating yummy food with friends and family, and the outdoors (especially horseback riding at Hickory Nut Gap Farm or jumping into one of our beautiful mountain swimming holes!). I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had to travel abroad and learn about other cultures. I feel extremely fortunate to have been born and raised in such a wonderful community as Asheville. I love my hometown and all things about the Blue Ridge Mountains. 
My husband, Joe Ebel, is a Wisconsin native and has lived here in Asheville for 17 years. He is an an amazing musician, website developer, chef, handyman and just a great guy and fantastic husband! We manage several properties, all next door to us. We love the green space that surrounds us, the peacefulness of our setting, and the proximity to the downtown Asheville scene.

Joe and I met through music. We both write and perform. Between the two of us, we have five CDs of original, acoustic music. If you've seen the Ken Burns National Parks Series TV show on PBS, you've probably heard Joe's violin playing!
He also pays mandolin and acoustic and electric guitar.

Joe and I created a mission statement years ago, and it still holds:
'Create and sustain harmony and balance in ourselves and the world, through loving relationships, artful music, comfortable, peaceful environments and integrity of mind and body.'

name: Fabulous Studio 7 min to downtown!
description: This studio apartment is only a seven-minute drive to downtown Asheville. Situated at the end of a cul-de-sac, the acre and a half are filled with both flower and vegetable gardens, a large fire pit with plenty of seating (bring your bundle of firewood or ask if I can get for you at a small charge).
host_about:
My grandparents built this house in 1959. My grandfather was a Major General, head of the 13th AD, and a graduate of West Point in 1915, along with Eisenhower and Omar Bradley. After getting shot in WW2, his military career ended and he and my grandmother moved to Asheville so he could run the VA Hospital in Oteen. 

The house next door and three acres is what they bought in 1945 after witnessing a double rainbow over the mountains. After my mother and father moved us four kids to the upstairs of that house, my grandparents got an architect who studied with Frank Lloyd Wright to design the mid-century modern house next door, and my childhood was spent going between the houses. 

Four years ago I came up to renovate the place in order to sell it, but after watching a full moon rise over the mountains, I fell in love with it all over again and bought it. It's a comfort knowing this property has never left our family. I can feel all my relations here and enjoy the memories I had, mostly with my loving, brilliant, funny grandmother in this house. It has been a gathering spot for many famous people, including Ike and Mamie, who were close friends of my grandparents, and Carl Sandburg. 

I am an artistic welder and a singer and have travelled all over the world entertaining the troops for the Dept of Defense. host_about:
Traveling for pleasure, for me, is all about getting out of my routine  and exploring a destination, being outdoors, or simply just being in my own space.  I am a horrible tourist!  I would much rather be outside at a cafe observing people in the street than in a museum, and have learned to enjoy spontaneity on vacation or in an experience.  How else do you leave room for some amazing opportunities and perhaps fun stories later down the road?


Although I was raised in the Western North Carolina mountains, I left at a young age never thinking I would come back . . . EVER.  I have lived in many places and have had the privilege of some amazing  travel experiences internationally -  off the gringo path in Peru, living above an artist's gallery in Indonesia, going to school in the Loire Valley in France,  hiking into an active volcano in Nicaragua . . . the privilege was not about the places I stayed, but in the people I encountered who helped ignite my soul in some way or uncover what living is truly about. All of my travels and experiences have brought me back to this mystical and magical mountainous wonderland. And now I wish to share it with you!

host_about:
I love to travel and soak up as much local culture as I can wherever I go, so I decided to share my home with people like you that share this passion. 
  I grew up in Atlanta and discovered Asheville by way of Maui. I  lived on Maui and Kauai for a few years and when it came time to move back closer to family a Maui  friend suggested Asheville as an alternative to the big city.  He’d grown up in Chapel Hill and in Asheville. 
 So, after enough culture shock back in Atlanta I decided to explore Asheville in the late 90’s. After being here for a week or so wuth my Boxer Buddy I knew I'd found our new home.  I'd also developed a love of old houses growing up in Atlanta so bought this 1927 bungalow from a friend in 2000. 
 In 2006 I decided to create a new space with a view. Only by cleaning my gutters did I notice what a great view to the west there was from a slightly higher perspective. So, I designed and built the “Treetop Loft” and lived up there for many years and rented the downstairs long term. I now love sharing this space and hearing  feedback I get about the design, the light and feel of the space.
 I'm also artist and one of the reasons I moved back downstairs is to have more wall space for the larger paintings I'd missed. 
 I’m an avid motorcyclist, lover of the outdoors and great beer so Asheville has been the perfect home for a long time now! 

  I do hope you enjoy Asheville as much as I do !

In a city all about it's micro-neighborhoods, N. Lexington Avenue is The Neighborhood. This is the historic and cultural center of downtown Asheville, once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.

And on hip Lexington Ave., Apartment 201 at 80 LEX – a building once the town's feed and seed warehouse, now its hottest address – is THE place: a 1-bedroom, 1-bath apartment + one free parking space, that breathes Asheville chic.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

name: Enchanting Cottage near Downtown Asheville
description: Be immersed in the placid charm of this sun-soaked cottage, with its double height ceiling and back country atmosphere, yet 10 minutes from downtown Asheville and the Biltmore Estate. The nightly rate includes the cleaning fee to simplify booking. Sleeps 8 with 2 Queen beds and 4 singles in loft. The cleaning fee is included in the nightly price.
host_about:
After living in numerous places around the country, we are excited to return to our hometown of Asheville, and to share our family property.  Three of our four grown children live in Asheville, and our daughter, son-in-law and grandson live nearby on part of the eleven acre property.   Our sister (and co-host) Jenny lives in the log cabin on the property.  We like to open up our home to meet new people and let them experience the peacefulness and fun of mountain living.   I am a Financial Advisor with Earth Equity Advisors, headquartered in Asheville.  Our firm provides responsible investing and is a certified B Corporation, seeking to use business as a force for good. My husband Todd is an Anesthesist and works at Mission Hospital in Asheville.  We love to travel, and have been as far as New Zealand and Australia, and to Africa twice.  We are also avid hikers and enjoy the Great Smokies and travel to National Parks in the west. We are on a quest to hike in all the National Parks, and have been to 45 parks so far (out of 59). One of Todd's most exciting hikes was to the top of Half Dome in Yosemite and we just returned from visiting five of the eight National Parks in Alaska in August.

We started as Airbnb hosts at our lake house at Lake Norman six years ago, and have had wonderful guests---the people that stay with us have always been so respectful of our home, and often take great care to leave it in good shape.  When we have had the chance to meet our guests in person, it is such fun to learn about other people's travels and lives. name: 80 LEX 202 Iconic Downtown Location
description:
80 LEX Apartment 202 : Iconic Downtown Location 1 BD King / 1 BA private apartment at 80 N. Lexington Ave, includes one off street designated parking space, less than a block away.

They say that wherever you go, there you are.

We say, when you go to Asheville, this is where you want to be. Right here, in the heart of Asheville. Right here, on N. Lexington Ave., in a building once home to farmers and growers and today the heart of all things trendy, artsy and quintessential.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

name: 80 LEX 203 Eclectic Industrial Apt
description:
80 LEX Apartment 203 : 1 BD King / 1 BA 565 SQ FT private downtown apt at 80 N. Lexington Ave includes one free designated off street parking space a half a block away.

Embrace the unique charm of this boutique space in an iconic red brick property. The loft-inspired private apartment features exposed original walls, dark surfaces, contrasting textures and patterns, an array of unique furnishings, and curated artwork throughout.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

name: Rose Ranch Montford 1, central, private suite
description: Your room, light and cozy, with a private entrance and private bath, is part of our owner occupied Ranch style home. Can be rented in conjunction with "Rose Ranch Montford 2," allowing up to 2 additional guests. In Montford,  20 minute brisk, 30 minute leisurely, to downtown. Wonderful, friendly, diverse neighborhood, 2 blocks from the Historic Riverside Cemetery. Many trees and Victorian homes. Great for walking, running, biking and getting exercise!
host_about:
Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

name: Rose Ranch Montford 2, central, private suite
description: Your room, light and spacious, with a private entrance and private bath, is part of our owner occupied Ranch style home. Can be rented in conjunction with "Rose Ranch Montford 1," allowing up to 2 additional guests. 20 minute brisk, 30 minute leisurely, to downtown. Wonderful, friendly, diverse neighborhood, 2 blocks from the Historic Riverside Cemetery. Many trees and Victorian homes. Great for walking, running, biking and getting exercise!
host_about:
Born in NC, attended UNC-Chapel Hill and got a degree in Journalism. My mom's side of the family has lived in Western North Carolina for the past century and a half. I have relatives buried in the Riverside Cemetery, which we can see from our backyard.
However, I lived most of my adult life on the West Coast. After college, I drove west in a school bus and eventually landed outside Eugene, OR, next to a creek, grew lots of my food, and had a sewing business, selling at the Saturday Market, Circle of Hands and craft fairs up and down the West Coast.
I have been to all 50 states, Canada, several Central American countries, Caribbean islands and Europe. I LOVE meeting people from all around the world and have studied conflict resolution in large groups of people using World Work. I am a therapist full time, offering massage therapy as well as Bodywisdom Therapy, helping people unravel the messages of their bodies, at a location on Merrimon Avenue. I speak a bit of French and Spanish, but am alas, no longer fluent.
My son and I moved back to WNC several years ago to be near my Mom, who lives in Yancey County. I know some sweet areas to visit around the area and are including them in a notebook in the rooms. 
I love being able to offer people a centrally located place to enjoy what WNC has to offer, as well as a prime walking neighborhood to have access to downtown Asheville hotspots. 
I turned both bedrooms and bathrooms downstairs into places that I would like to visit myself, using art from my own collection, and textures and colors that I love.
We have friends and family over on a regular basis so there is a bit of hustle and bustle at times. If you have children, or like to come and go and appreciate the outdoors, you will fit right in! If you want privacy, the private entrance and keypad will fit your needs. If you want total peace and quiet, I am afraid we won't be your cup of tea.
Living lightly on the earth is a core value for me so we recycle as much as possible, and keep our throwaway consumables to a minimum. 
Life is for loving, sharing and making the world better wherever we can.

name: Chicken Pie Alley, walkable to downtown
description: Welcome to our private downstairs apartment that has been lovingly renovated to offer easy comfort minutes from the heart of downtown Asheville. Nestled on a quiet cottage lane, our space offers a clean, welcoming and private space that is easy walking to coffee houses, pubs, restaurants and the civic center (4 blocks away).
host_about:
We are a small little family of three, me, my husband, Rick, and our 12 yr old daughter, Trinity lane. We have lived in Asheville since our daughter was born and love it! I'm a licensed professional counselor and Rick is on Ski patrol at Cataloochee ski resort and a fly fishing guide. We chose to fix up a historic bungalow right on the edge of town so that we could walk everywhere. We have recently completing the basement to create our own airbnb space. 

We love to travel like locals, having unique experiences connecting to people where ever we go. We are action oriented people who can also appreciate being pampered a bit. name: High-Design Downtown Loft
description: Over 1,300 square-feet and two loft bedrooms, 33 Carolina Lane – a block once dedicated to agricultural industry, today a multi-cultural gathering spot – offers modern amenities and industrial design, with just the right touch of history: Curated artwork and pops of color, designer furnishings and massive flat-screen TVs, exposed ducts and lofted ceilings – all, in perfect balance with wizened walls and striking wood floors, layered with the patina of the past.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

In appreciation for the kindness shown to us over the years, we pay it forward by being clean and courteous when we are guests in the homes of others, and we are seeking to host guests who are similarly self-sufficient and simply seeking a basic place for the night.

We look forward to you staying in our home!

name: The Woodfin - Chateau de Bro & Chalet de Bae
description:
THE SPACE IS ALL YOURS!

The Woodfin is a chateau de bro, chalet de bae, camp for champs, and home for the roaming adventurer. Nestled in a quiet neighborhood just a 5 to 7-minute drive from downtown, this private dream pad is the perfect hub for couples, friends, and family to explore everything Asheville. host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

name: 1920s bungalow near river, 8 min drive to AVL
description: This convenient, eclectic, industrial neighborhood is located about 8 minutes from the heart of downtown Asheville!  Across from the house is The Mill at Riverside, complete with local artists' studios and High Five Coffee Shop. Just up the way is Woodfin Riverside Park, located directly on the French Broad River with waterside benches and a pedestrian path. You'll be so close to water activities such as floating, paddle boarding, kayaking, and fishing during the warmer months.
host_about:
Hello and thank you for checking out my profile! I'm a superhost from Asheville, NC who enjoys to travel, hike, ski, and love on my two pugs. 

An original Floridian, I traded the beach for the mountains back in 2008. I've visited western North Carolina all of my life and finally decided to call Asheville home after graduating from Florida State University. I moved here knowing one person and had no job lined up, but it was the best decision I've ever made. Since then, I've had the opportunity to buy my first house in West Asheville, achieve my MBA from Western Carolina University, and work for the Biltmore Estate for over a decade! 

I am honored to have the opportunity to share my love of Asheville with others as they visit this magical town- some come over and over again while others are experiencing it for the very first time. Whether you're here to explore these majestic mountains, attend a special event, hike the Appalachian Trail, visit the Biltmore Estate, or float down the French Broad River, I am thrilled to host you during your time here!

name: Elegant + Edgy Loft
description:
King & Queen + 2 Full Bathrooms + Fully Stocked Kitchen + 1,300 sq. ft Private Residential Loft + One Free Off Street Parking

Secreted into the heart of the city – an industrial 2-bedroom loft, cloaked within the confines of a one-way alley, long known only to the real Asheville. A block once devoted to agriculture, today ensconced within the multicultural vibe of downtown. A modern-yet-historic, industrial-while-inviting, convenient-but-secluded (as cities go) kind of place.
host_about:
Growing up Santa Fe, NM I saw a unique blend of artistic community, endless outdoor opportunities, interesting history, beautiful landscapes, and a diverse mix of cultures.

Though far from Santa Fe and a different climate, I arrived in Asheville in the early 90’s to practice Chinese Medicine and felt some of the same elements at play.  Asheville was not well known, but you could feel the energy building and the mixture of art, landscape, environment, history and community all coming together.  It reminded me of my ‘early days’ in Santa Fe.  

One of my closest friends was Andy Brokmeyer, who I told for several years that he needed to come to Asheville, as it was a dynamic and exciting place.  We were also avid kayakers, and Asheville has been a Mecca for kayaking since the early days of the sport so I knew I could lure him out with the promise of all the great rivers in the area. 

He came out ‘for a visit’ and hasn’t left.  That was 16 years ago.  

Asheville has grown into the most happening place in the region, far beyond my expectations, and has sustained an authentic, community oriented and dynamic quality.  Like my dad used to say about few places, it has ‘cultural energy’. 

Though both Andy and I had done some residential real estate investment and development, 80 N Lexington was our first move into the commercial side.  It was an old building, greatly in need of repair, and was a bit removed from the core downtown commercial traffic.  We scraped together what we could and fixed it up, with an eye towards something special in the future. 
 
Now, many years later, North Lexington Ave is hopping, with restaurants, breweries, bars, tea houses, coffee shops, galleries and wonderful, diverse retail shops right out the door.  

And 80 N Lexington has been transformed into a blend of funky, hip, and industrial intertwined with lush, upscale design.  A mix of style and comfort that is unique and authentically Asheville.  

Just like Asheville, there’s nothing quite like it.

name: Upstream Bachelor Sanctuary - New Wedding Venue
description: RIVER VIEWS! Perfect for large groups and gatherings, this spacious modern eco-friendly riverfront home is located next to Asheville’s River Arts District and just minutes from the popular West AVL and Downtown. Enjoy mountain views, a rooftop hot tub, and plenty of room to gather, or relax and unwind. Walk to breweries, restaurants, galleries, and the Greenway, or relax riverside at Carrier Park! The iconic Biltmore Estate is just a skip away! Convenient, scenic, and ideal for group stays.
host_about:
Our houses are much nicer than they appear on this site.   Airbnb does not allow us to use our own photographs on two of our listings so you may need to go on our internal website.   It is easy to find us with a simple search for "Upstream way"   That is the name of our street.

We also have lots of cool video and virtual tours.   Lesley, my right hand, has compiled volumes of information on Asheville and travel tips for your visit.

Anyone who uses Airbnb knows you have to invest a lot of time and energy to find the good rentals in Asheville, NC.   The city made it illegal after we got our permits and there are way too many folks trying to book far too few homes.    

We built our new website so you will not get tricked with photoshop.    Our 5 houses on Upstream Way are the real thing.   

My development company built the whole street so we are not like a normal house you find in a random location next door to owner occupied homes in a residential neighborhood.   

I have stayed in those before and you are not exactly welcomed by the other homeowners.   The neighbors tend to dislike the constant coming and going of tourists in a family neighborhood.

I once lived next to an illegal Airbnb property and came up with a solution.

We are literally an entire resort of vacation rentals all side by side.   Your neighbor is also here for a special occasion and will probably offer you a beverage.

You can bring anywhere from 1 to 100 people and have the whole place to yourself.

It is without equal.   The best you can do is copy us, but nobody can get the permits.

Bachelorette’s and Wedding Parties got us started but we shy away from them now.   

We will host a lot of different occasions and you need not worry if you want to have a bachelor party or bachelorette.   

I make it no secret that we want to focus on corporate executives who visit for team building and holistic health retreats, but we don't judge your motive.

We welcome everyone the same way.

You can depend on us because we deliver what you are expecting and then we go as far beyond as is humanly possible.

My team has some of the best and brightest.   My right hand is Lesley, my left hand is Aracely, her children Kasey and Brian are her right and left hands.  If something needs repair, Leo & Kaden are available.

I have known each person on my staff from years and years of time together.   I am not easy to work for.   Trust me.   

At times, I have no idea why these people are such hard workers and trusted friends. 
With Covid-19 we all work for a fraction of our former compensation.

Somehow; you and I both got lucky.    We survived this and I see the light at the end of the tunnel.

Ok, I will wrap this up:

If you reach out you will never get an answering service or a stranger.   

We are not property managers.    We are the folks who built this place.

We built it for you.

You don't arrive here by accident.

So far, 217 Airbnb customers have reviewed us.   Keep in mind, that represents thousands of people as our average group is 12 people.

Nobody has ever given us below 5 stars.   Not even once.   Not even close.

Plus, you are welcome to check a lot of other websites and our own internal software.  

Thousands of people have come here and they seem to be happy with us and we often see them again and again.

We cost more for a reason:   

You get more.

You come for a special occasion.   

You leave with a priceless memory.

Then we plan for the next one.

I think that is why we are almost booked out into '22.

All the best,
jay

name: The Madera Madre - Made for Asheville Living
description: The Madera Madre - the “mother wood” gives life to the visceral vacationer and warmth to the weary traveler. Settle in with ease to your home away from home, nestled in a quiet neighborhood just a 5 to 7-minute drive from downtown. This private dream pad is the ideal hub for couples, friends, and family to explore everything Asheville. Recharge in the high-end Serta iComfort® bed with adjustable frame for an unbeatable night’s sleep! Fully equipped kitchen. Professionally cleaned!!
host_about:
I grew up on the Texas border near South Padre Island. I moved to Asheville in (Phone number hidden by Airbnb) from Austin, TX soon after graduating with a degree in mechanical engineering. The mountains called my name, and my would-be manager also called my name (to offer me a job),  so I set out on the 17hr drive and only looked back once...because I thought I saw a bear.

 I began my career servicing CTs, MRIs, and X-ray systems throughout Western North Carolina. If I'm not working on the house or hanging with the fam, my free time is spent playing outdoors - kayak fishing, mountain biking, and rock climbing. 

If there's an opportunity to go fishing, I usually take the bait. I own a small fleet of fishing kayaks and like to take day trips out on the local waters to pursue bass, trout and gorgeous scenery. If you're in the neighborhood to catch some fish, let me know and Ill try to give you some tips on where to go. 

Asheville is a mountain biker's paradise. There's an expansive network of trail systems all throughout the surrounding forests lands and hitting the trails with the gang is a surefire way to put a smile on my face. IMO its the best way to submerse yourself in these mountains and take in all their beauty. If you're itching for a thrilling downhill adventure or a casual bike ride through the mountains, reach out and I can point you in the right direction. 

My relationship with rock climbing is fickle; I'm either climbing or I'm not. I love it because by nature it puts you by nature. But if the fish are biting, its hard to pull me from a kayak to climb a 300 ft bluff. 

I also love music, food, and beer. If Asheville's beer and culinary scene is what brought you here, I am happy to offer advice. Let me know!

description:
5-star 1960s unique mountain cottage that is just 1.2 miles from downtown Asheville. Located on Beaucatcher Mountain, this charming home sits on a narrow switchback road above the famous mountain tunnel heading into downtown Asheville.

host_about:
Our family visited Asheville, NC, during one of our sightseeing tours across the United States, and we instantly fell in love with the city - so much so that we decided to purchase a vacation house there!  And the minute we stepped inside the Zurich Swiss Chalet property, we knew it was the one. 

Our adorable chalets combine our love for serene, picturesque getaways with our desire to remain close to the city's restaurants and shops. Because of how lovely it is and its unique location within the City of Asheville, we decided to share it with others.  

Hopefully, you'll enjoy it as much as we do!

Love + Gratitude = Peace

I grew up in India, a land of diverse languages, cultures, and terrain, and lived in the United States as a software engineer all my adult life working and traveling. I have been a wanderlust all my life. I enjoy traveling to new places, meeting new people, trying new cuisines, and experiencing different cultures.

Devo Bhava means God-like. Thus, Atithi Devo Bhava indicates that we must consider our guests equivalent to God and care for them.

Feel free to book or message me first; I am friendly, outgoing, and happy to answer any specific questions in advance.

I am a well-traveled guest who knows what hosts should do to create a comfortable experience. My goal is to fulfill these requirements for every guest.

Hope to host you soon!

When you are a guest in our cabin homes you are provided with clean, comfortable accommodations in a caring heart centered energetically beneficial environment. Your payment is considered a donation to the charity and supports  the continuation of youth empowerment programs. 

Love + Gratitude = Peace

Love + Gratitude = Peace

host_about:
I am grateful everyday for the opportunity to walk and breath on this earth.  There are so many nooks and crannies to explore on this planet; I would be arrogant to think that I can see them all!  

Nevertheless, it is challenging for me to think of anything more exhilarating and exciting than travelling to a new place--whether its seeing the same sun rise from a different perspective, the same water cascading down a different waterfall, or the same rock weathered differently by aeons of storms, this beautiful planet is always different, yet always the same.  

Like wise, there is something incredibly spiritual about meeting a new person with an uniquely individual and unforgettable personality, stimulating conversation, and the realisation that there is really nothing that separates us on this earth.

If I stay somewhere, whether it's someone's house, or camping in the middle of the woods, it's a little piece of the same planet, so I will treat it with respect and love, and try to leave as small a foot-print there as possible.
